newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges Kabila to prevent suffering in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France urges Kabila to prevent suffering in Zaire.

text.p: France warned rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Monday that relying on force to seize control of Kinshasa would condemn Zaireans to additional suffering.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt insisted that a peaceful transfer of power was still possible and said that "those who would pass up this opportunity and rely instead on force would condemn the Zairean people to new suffering".
Rummelhardt, speaking to reporters during a regular ministry briefing, did not mention Kabila by name.
He again urged French nationals in Zaire to leave for the time being if their presence was not indispensable.
Defence Minister Charles Millon, answering questions in Lyon, central France, said Paris was concerned by the situation but reaffirmed it would not intervene in Zairean affairs.
Kabila's rebels have said that peace talks set for Wednesday would be Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's last chance to make a peaceful exit from power.

The rebels, who now control three quarters of the country, said they were fighting their way towards the capital Kinshasa under their new policy of coupling military pressure with diplomatic attempts to avert bloodshed in the city.
Kabila will meet Mobutu aboard the South African navy ship the Outeniqua off Congo on Wednesday for a second round of negotiations.
